questions.question: Which of the two signs should be interchanged in the following equation to make the given value correct? 15 + 5 - 10 × 6 ÷ 12 = 6
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the two signs should be interchanged in the following equation to make the given value correct?

15 + 5 - 10 × 6 ÷ 12 = 6
questions.solution:
Interchanging - and ÷

\(15 + 5 \div 10 \times 6 - 12 = 15 + \frac{{5 \times 6}}{{10}} - 12\)

15 + 3 - 12 = 6

Interchanging + and ÷

15 ÷ 5 – 10 × 6 + 12 = 3 - 60 + 12

15 – 60 ≠ 6

Interchanging + and ×

\(15 \times 5 - 10 + 6 \div 12 = 75 - 10 + \frac{1}{2}\)

\(65 + \frac{1}{2} \ne 6\)

Interchanging + and -

15 - 5 + 10 × 6 ÷ 12 = 15 - 5 + 5

15 – 5 ≠ 6

Hence by interchanging - and ÷ we get the correct equation.

questions.questionHtml: A boat can cover a distance of 7.2 km downstream and 3.2 km upstream in 2 hours. It can also cover 1.5 km downstream and 0.6 km upstream in 24 minutes. What is the speed of the boat when going downstream (in km/h)?
questions.solution:
Let the speed of the boat be x km/hr and the speed of the stream be y km/hr.

∴ Speed of boat in downstream = (x + y) km/hr

∴ Speed of boat in upstream = (x – y) km/hr

According to the question

\(\Rightarrow \frac{7.2}{\text{x}+\text{y}}+\frac{3.2}{\text{x}-\text{y}}=2\)

\(\Rightarrow \frac{1.5}{\text{x}+\text{y}}+\frac{0.6}{\text{x}-\text{y}}=\frac{24}{60}\)

Suppose 1/(x + y) = a, and 1/(x – y) = b, then

⇒ 7.2a + 3.2b = 2

⇒ 0.9a + 0.4b = 2/8 = 1/4      ----(1)

⇒ 1.5a + 0.6b = 2/5

⇒ 0.5a + 0.2b = 2/15      ----(2)

Multiply by 2 in equation (2)

⇒ a + 0.4b = 4/15      ----(3)

Subtract equation (1) from (3)

⇒ 0.1a = 1/60

⇒ a = 1/6

⇒ 1/(x + y) = 1/6

∴ Speed of the boat in downstream is 6 km/hr.

questions.question: If a 10-digit number 1330x558y2 is divisible by 88, then the value of (x + y) is:
questions.questionHtml: If a 10-digit number 1330x558y2 is divisible by 88, then the value of (x + y) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For divisibility by 88, the number must be divisible by both 8 and 11.

For divisibility by 8, the last three digits 8y2 must be divisible by 8 → y = 3 (as 832 ÷ 8 = 104).

For divisibility by 11, the difference between sum of odd position digits and even position digits must be 0 or a multiple of 11.

Sum of odd positions (1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th, 9th) = 1 + 3 + x + 5 + y = 9 + x + y = 12 + x (since y = 3).

Sum of even positions (2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th, 10th) = 3 + 0 + 5 + 8 + 2 = 18.

To make (18) − (12 + x) = 0 → 6 − x = 0 → x = 6.

Thus, x + y = 6 + 3 = 9.

∴ The correct answer is 9.

Alternate Method

Given: The 10-digit number is 1330x558y2 and it is divisible by 88.

Formula Used:

A number is divisible by 88 if it is divisible by both 8 and 11 (co-prime factors of 88).

Divisibility rule of 8: Last 3 digits must be divisible by 8.

Divisibility rule of 11: Absolute difference of the sum of digits at odd places and even places must be 0 or divisible by 11.

Calculations:

⇒ Divisibility by 8 check: last three digits = 8y2

⇒ For y = 3, 832 ÷ 8 = 104 (completely divisible)

⇒ Therefore, y = 3

⇒ The 10-digit number becomes 1330x55832

⇒ Divisibility by 11 check:

⇒ Sum of digits at odd places = 1 + 3 + x + 5 + 3 = 12 + x

⇒ Sum of digits at even places = 3 + 0 + 5 + 8 + 2 = 18

⇒ Difference = 18 − (12 + x) = 6 − x

⇒ For the difference to be 0, 6 − x = 0

⇒ x = 6

⇒ Value of (x + y) = 6 + 3 = 9

∴ The correct answer is 9.

Additional Information

Divisibility Rule of 8

A number is divisible by 8 if the number formed by its last three digits is divisible by 8, or if the last three digits are all zeros.

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the absolute difference between the sum of the digits at odd positions and the sum of the digits at even positions is 0 or a multiple of 11.

Composite Divisibility

To check divisibility by a composite number like 88, express it as a product of co-prime numbers (e.g., 8 × 11). The number must be divisible by each of these co-prime factors.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select No improvement. He came late, wasn't it ?
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select No improvement.

He came late, wasn't it?
questions.solution:
• Tag questions are made using an auxiliary verb (for example: be or have) and a subject pronoun (for example I, you, she).
  • Usually if the main clause is positive, the question tag is negative, and if the main clause is negative, it's positive.
    For example
    • It's cold (positive), isn't it (negative)?
    • It isn't cold (negative), is it (positive)?
  • If the main clause has an auxiliary verb in it, you use the same verb in the tag question. If there is no auxiliary verb (in the present simple and past simple) use do/does/ did (just like when you make a normal question). That is why the question tag here is --didn’t he? ('he' according to subject)
     

​Thus, the correct sentence is: He came late, didn't he?

questions.question: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. She forgot lock the door when she went out in a hurry.
questions.questionHtml:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

She forgot lock the door when she went out in a hurry.
questions.solution:
The --She forgot lock-- part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect.

The correct phrase that should be used here is ---She forgot to lock--. The infinitive form of the verb --lock-- should be used.

Basically, an infinitive verb is a verb with the word to in front of it.

  • to be

  • to have

  • to hold

  • to sleep

  • to dream

When you use an infinitive verb, --to--- is a part of the verb. It is not acting as a preposition in this case. And the verb is always just the verb. It's not conjugated in any way - no -ed, no -ing, no -s on the end.

There are several possible ways to use infinitive verbs. You can use them:

  1. as the subject of a sentence - To err is human; to forgive, divine.

  2. like an adjective or adverb phrase that expresses purpose or intent - My instructions are to press this button every hour.

  3. following an indirect object - He told me to give this to you.

  4. following certain other verbs:

  • afford - We can't afford to eat out every night.

  • agree - Let's agree to disagree.

  • aim - I aim to please.

Hence the correct answer is option 1.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Lock, stock and barrel
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Lock, stock and barrel
questions.solution:
The correct answer is completely

Key Points

  • Lock, stock, and the barrel is a figure of speech used predominantly in the United Kingdom and North America, meaning all, total, everything.
  • The effective portions of a gun (or more specifically a musket) are the lock (used to hold ready the sparking mechanism), the stock (the portion held), and the barrel (the aiming guide and conveyor for the explosive-driven projectile). Collectively they are the whole weapon, and therefore everything.

questions.question: Select the correct active form of the given sentence. One of the passengers was being thoroughly checked by the customs officers.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.

One of the passengers was being thoroughly checked by the customs officers.

options.text: The customs officers thoroughly checked one of the passengers.

questions.solution:
The structures for both the active and passive forms for past continuous tense are given below:

  • Active form- Subject +was/were + V1 + ing + Object
  • Passive form- Object + was/were + being + V3 + by + Subject
     

The given sentence is an assertive one and in the passive voice form.

  • Follow the active form structure for the past continuous tense given above:
    • Exchange the places of the subject and object. (One of the passengers - the custom officers)
  • At last line up the remaining part
     

Following these steps, we finally get- The customs officers were thoroughly checking one of the passengers.

Key Points  

  • In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
  • In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
  • The given sentence is in the active voice.
  • When we convert this sentence into passive voice, we use the verb 'request' instead of the adverb ';please'.
  • The passive format "are + V3" should be used.
  • This is the active and passive voice rule for the present simple tense.
  • Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Hence the answer is You are requested to take these students round the biscuit factory.

questions.question: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. Lodi Colony in Delhi is very different from other places in the city that is crowded and noisy.
questions.questionHtml:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Lodi Colony in Delhi is very different from other places in the city that is crowded and noisy.
questions.solution:
The that is crowded and noisy part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect.

The correct phrase that should be used here is-- that are crowded and noisy. The Subject-Verb agreement rule is not followed here.

Subjects and verbs must AGREE with one another in number (singular or plural). Thus, if a subject is singular, its verb must also be singular; if a subject is a plural, its verb must also be plural. Other places is plural, hence the verb that follows it must also be plural- --are.

the correct sentence is- Lodi Colony in Delhi is very different from other places in the city that are crowded and noisy.

Hence the correct answer is option 2.
